We live in a world of constant balancing, a sustaining while fragile process all over the places. Too much income gap would lead to public unrest, while too little difference among people will discourage inventions and creations. Such is the fundamental struggle of Hacknet. A world of anonymity, security, tracing and breaking ins. It should be known, as the game argues in its gameplay and story, that none of these parties should hold an upperhand in real life: complete anonymity incentivize cyber-crimes, while complete transparency would only guide to even more societal problems and loss of motivations.
The main advantage of Hacknet is its ability to exploit its game system to create a deep and dense world using as little materials as possible. Such is the idea of hacking, as players are constantly aware that he/she could only gain a small portion of the whole perspective. Players are forced to interpret the story based on little to no information. The storytelling, in a unique format, is comstantly immersive, and perhaps only achieved with such a creative gaming system.
Admittedly, the game might not be for everyone. The system it uses is complex, and the tutorial rather not intuitive, which narrows its main consumers to those who have at least some knowledge in linux or programming languages. This, however, should not taunt any prospective players, and I would recommend anyone to try it out.

Personally, I enjoyed this game in the sense that I feel so much more comfortable using DOSbox for playing some games like Daggerfall, The Lost Vikings, Ultima, etc. Playing a game that gives you some form of skill to take away from it AND have fun is something that not many games can offer. 

I'm a sucker for the soundtrack, too. If you like playing games with great music, this game has what you need. Honestly, if you are stuck, it's not bad to look up something to help, but only if you tried something and it didn't work. 9 times out of 10, when I looked something up I was stumped on, I never needed to look it up again, because it would easily translate into what I've done before. There really isn't that much commands to memorize and use anyway, so it's not that bad. 

If I were you, I'd do the Labyrinths DLC asap, because the tools you get from that dlc are by far better than the mainline game's tools. I'm still playing this game for now, I just thought I'd give my 2 cents on this game so STEAM will stop bugging me to rate it. Hope you like the game.

Hacknet is a really good puzzle game with an amazing soundtrack. The mechanics are fun to learn, even if some are very similar, and the gameplay is rewarding as you earn more "hacks". The game is not for everyone, but if you are into this sort of thing then it is a ton of fun. Just don't put down the game and expect to jump right back into it weeks or months later. There is a learning curve for sure.

I am very interested in learning about computer science, and also frequently get lost in puzzle games like those developed by Zachtronics. To the best of my knowledge, this game scratches the latter itch while giving the illusion of scratching the former. While this game may touch on some fundamentals of command line syntax and internet privacy, it is mostly for entertainment purposes. I have not been at all disappointed with this game, and will definitely end up finishing it, as it has been the most immersive game that I have ever played by far. I was absolutely not expecting to experience any sort of adrenaline rush from a puzzle game, and in some ways it has been as exciting as a playthrough of DOOM. 4th wall breaks are not even necessary, as the game is a fairly convincing simulation of a console, and getting attacked by another "user" definitely caught me off guard more than once. Following a seemingly unsuspecting file down a rabbit hole is extremely satisfying once you get to the end and realize that it was only a tangential easter egg separate from the main quests of the game. It is definitely not for everyone, but finding this game tucked away in a forgotten humble bundle was a pleasant surprise.
